Mechanistic plausibility (osmolality drives vasopressin which drives cAMP-mediated cyst growth) supports continued prospective evaluation, but this finding should not be used to recommend forced fluid intake outside trial settings. Complementary to existing finding_009 (water intake). RELATIONSHIP TO TOLVAPTAN: finding is in tolvaptan-naive patients, so does not directly inform on-treatment monitoring.

findings.statement: Pregnancy was not associated with ADPKD progression in a secondary analysis of HALT-PKD (Lapierre-Nguyen et al., JASN May 2026). Among 455 women in HALT-PKD A+B, having 1-2 or 3+ prior pregnancies was not significantly associated with eGFR slope, percentage TKV change, or a composite kidney failure outcome. In-study pregnancy (n=13, propensity-matched 1:4) also showed a null result (eGFR slope Beta: -0.14, 95% CI -2.72 to 2.44). This is a NEGATIVE/NULL result with HIGH counseling relevance — but note that the in-study pregnancy arm is very small (n=13), with wide confidence intervals that cannot rule out a clinically meaningful effect.

evolution.note: New finding from Lapierre-Nguyen et al. (JASN May 2026, pm_42149684; ALERT generated 2026-05-19). Secondary analysis of HALT-PKD Study A and B data. Development cohort: n=455 women with early ADPKD (HALT-A: eGFR 60-89, HALT-B: eGFR 25-60). Prior pregnancies (1-2 or 3+) were not significantly associated with eGFR slope (multivariable-adjusted), dTKV/year, or a composite kidney failure outcome. In-study pregnancy subgroup: n=13 propensity-matched 1:4 to non-pregnant women; eGFR slope Beta -0.14 (95% CI -2.72 to 2.44) — null result. Importance 8/Evidence 5/Novelty 8/Decision 8/Calibration 7. CLASSIFICATION: practice-relevant (counseling). WHY THIS MATTERS: Pregnancy in ADPKD has historically generated concern about accelerating progression, based on case series and small observational studies suggesting higher proteinuria and blood pressure during pregnancy. This HALT-PKD secondary analysis is the largest and most rigorous dataset to date addressing this question with longitudinal outcomes data. A null result with this dataset is reassuring. CRITICAL LIMITATIONS: (1) The in-study pregnancy arm n=13 is very small — the 95% CI (-2.72 to 2.44 mL/min/1.73m²/yr) is wide and does not exclude a clinically meaningful negative effect; this is statistically inconclusive for the in-study pregnancy analysis. (2) HALT-PKD enrolled patients with relatively preserved eGFR (most >60 in Study A); the reassurance may not extend to patients with more advanced CKD. (3) HALT-PKD participants were mostly Caucasian, non-diabetic, and enrolled at US academic centers — generalizability to more diverse populations is uncertain. (4) The analysis addresses kidney progression specifically; it does not address obstetric outcomes (preeclampsia, gestational hypertension, preterm birth) or other pregnancy complications in ADPKD patients, which remain relevant to counseling. (5) This is a secondary analysis of a trial not designed for this purpose. CONFIDENCE: moderate — the prior-pregnancy multivariable analysis is reasonably well-powered and reassuring; the in-study pregnancy analysis is underpowered. DECISION VALUE: high for counseling purposes, with the explicit caveat above.

findings.statement: GLPG2737 (a CFTR inhibitor, 150 mg/day) showed no significant effect on htTKV growth rate (GLPG2737 +8.2% vs placebo +9.2%, difference −0.91%, p=0.61) or eGFR slope (difference −2.31 mL/min/1.73 m², p=0.17) in a Phase 2a RCT (MANGROVE, NCT04578548, n=66, 52 weeks). The trial was terminated early for lack of efficacy. This definitively prunes CFTR channel inhibition with GLPG2737 from the near-term ADPKD pipeline and materially weakens the broader CFTR-mediated chloride secretion hypothesis as a standalone disease-modifying approach in typical adult ADPKD.

evolution.note: New finding from MANGROVE Phase 2a RCT (Gansevoort et al., NDT May 2026, pm_42201338; ALERT generated 2026-05-28). Phase 2a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, 2:1 allocation. GLPG2737 150 mg/day vs placebo, n=66, 52 weeks. Primary: htTKV growth rate — GLPG2737 +8.2% vs placebo +9.2%, difference −0.91%, p=0.61 (not significant). Secondary: eGFR change difference −2.31 mL/min/1.73 m², p=0.17 (not significant). Well tolerated. Trial and companion OLE terminated early for lack of efficacy. Companion preclinical paper (Ganapathy et al., Am J Nephrol Apr 2025, pm_40300563) showed GLPG2737 prevents cyst growth in multiple mouse models and human ADPKD kidney cells — the clinical failure is consistent with ADPKD's poor preclinical-to-clinical translation record. LIMITATIONS: n=66 Phase 2a, powered for surrogate endpoint not patient-important outcomes; single dose tested; does not exclude different doses, other CFTR modulators, or combination regimens with tolvaptan; CFTR non-channel scaffold/HIPPO-pathway interactions (pm_42140432, Sharma et al.) represent a distinct mechanistic angle not tested by GLPG2737. NOTE: trial completed April 2023, full publication occurred May 2026 (~3-year lag — a pattern consistent with delayed publication of negative trials). DECISION VALUE: HIGH — adds CFTR inhibition to the list of mechanistically plausible but clinically failed approaches in ADPKD (alongside pravastatin, venglustat, somatostatin analogues for kidney disease). Industry-funded study (Galapagos) but a clean well-calibrated negative with no commercial incentive to inflate.

findings.statement: ADPKD patients on kidney replacement therapy (KRT) have independently lower dialysis mortality compared to other causes of kidney failure (aHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.67-0.75; ANZDATA registry, n=63,875), with similar post-transplant survival (aHR 0.96) and slightly better kidney allograft survival (aHR 0.87). This likely reflects ADPKD patients' younger age at KRT initiation and lower comorbidity burden rather than a disease-specific protective effect. Causes of death on KRT are similar including cardiovascular disease (~27.5%).

evolution.note: New finding from Jefferis et al. (BMC Nephrology Sep 2025, pm_41023960; surfaced in scan_2026-05-23, is_new_this_week=false). ANZDATA Registry retrospective cohort: n=63,875 patients commencing KRT in Australia between 1963-2020, including n=2,466 ADPKD. ADPKD vs non-ADPKD KRT: all-cause mortality on dialysis aHR 0.71 (95% CI 0.67-0.75); post-transplant mortality aHR 0.96 (not significantly different); kidney allograft survival aHR 0.87 (slightly better in ADPKD). Cardiovascular death rates similar (27.5% ADPKD vs 27.6% non-ADPKD). Importance 5/Evidence 5/Novelty 5/Decision 4/Calibration 8. CLASSIFICATION: background/context. INTERPRETATION: ADPKD patients reaching KRT tend to be younger and have fewer diabetes and cardiovascular comorbidities than KRT patients with other etiologies — the lower dialysis mortality likely reflects this case-mix advantage rather than any ADPKD-specific protective mechanism. The similar cardiovascular death proportion (despite lower overall mortality) suggests cardiovascular risk is not reduced in ADPKD, consistent with ADPKD's known cardiovascular complications (hypertension, LVH, intracranial aneurysms, aortic dilation). LIMITATIONS: retrospective registry data; ANZDATA covers Australia/New Zealand only; long enrollment period (1963-2020) spans major changes in KRT practice; case-mix confounding is the dominant limitation; no adjustment for disease severity at KRT initiation. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: supports counseling patients that ADPKD outcomes after reaching KRT are generally favorable relative to other KRT populations. This does not diminish the severity of ADPKD or the importance of delaying KRT initiation.

findings.statement: CT-confirmed nephrolithiasis (kidney stones), distinguished from cyst-wall calcification, is independently associated with a higher risk of initiating renal replacement therapy in ADPKD. In the prospective Korean HOPE-PKD cohort (n=410, median follow-up 5.18 years), imaging-confirmed nephrolithiasis carried an adjusted HR of 2.84 (95% CI 1.26-6.38) for RRT initiation and 1.83 (1.03-3.27) for a composite progression outcome. This supports considering CT-detected kidney stones as an additional prognostic marker alongside Mayo imaging class and genotype, but does not establish that treating stones alters kidney outcomes, and the association may reflect stones as a marker of more severe underlying disease rather than a causal driver of progression.

evolution.note: New finding from pm_42428517 (Clinical Kidney Journal, 2026-06-11), the first prospective, imaging-confirmed assessment of nephrolithiasis as an ADPKD progression risk factor with a patient-important endpoint (prior evidence was retrospective). LIMITATIONS: observational (cannot establish causation), only 51 RRT events drove a wide confidence interval, the composite secondary endpoint's lower bound (1.03) barely excluded the null, single baseline CT exposure assessment, single-country cohort, and one author reports a Korea Otsuka Pharmaceutical (tolvaptan manufacturer) research grant unrelated to the analyzed exposure. Confidence set to LOW pending replication in an independent cohort; clinical relevance rated MODERATE because kidney stones are common and potentially modifiable, even though causal benefit of stone treatment on kidney survival is unproven.

findings.statement: A cross-cutting methodological question emerged this cycle about whether creatinine-based eGFR is a reliable primary endpoint for ADPKD drug trials. Three independent threads converge: (1) a perspective preprint hypothesizes that tolvaptan-related changes in creatinine generation may have inflated the apparent creatinine-eGFR benefit in TEMPO 3:4, while informative censoring from selective discontinuation may have simultaneously attenuated it, and proposes an (as-yet-unperformed) cystatin C reanalysis; (2) the LIPS lanreotide RCT found a significant creatinine-based eGFR treatment signal that was NOT reproduced by cystatin C-eGFR or urinary creatinine clearance in the same trial; (3) separate retrospective comparisons show that eGFR equation choice (creatinine vs. cystatin C vs. combined; 2009 vs. 2021 race-free CKD-EPI) meaningfully shifts calculated eGFR and CKD staging in ADPKD cohorts, with the combined creatinine-cystatin C equation best approximating measured GFR. None of these individually change practice, but together they raise a testable, currently unresolved question about whether some historical ADPKD trial results relying on creatinine-eGFR could be biased, and argue for cystatin C or measured-GFR co-reporting in future ADPKD trials.

evolution.note: New cross-dimensional finding created this cycle to track a thematically convergent but individually inconclusive set of items: ppr_1279948 (hypothesis-only, no new data, not peer-reviewed), pm_42519961 (single-center retrospective, mGFR-validated subset n=50), and pm_42499441 (retrospective recalculation exercise, no outcome data). None constitutes strong evidence alone; the value is in the convergence, and in cross-referencing the LIPS RCT's internal creatinine/cystatin C discordance (see finding_019). Confidence LOW and clinical relevance MODERATE -- this should raise research priority (a formal TEMPO 3:4 cystatin C reanalysis would be genuinely informative) without changing today's clinical practice, which still correctly relies on creatinine-eGFR as the practical standard. Watchlist item: whether any group performs the proposed TEMPO 3:4 reanalysis.

findings.statement: In a large US national registry analysis, peritoneal dialysis (PD) was associated with lower mortality and higher likelihood of subsequent kidney transplantation compared to hemodialysis (HD) among ADPKD patients reaching end-stage kidney disease. This is retrospective, non-randomized, observational evidence subject to substantial confounding by indication -- PD-selected patients were younger, more often female, and had lower comorbid disease burden -- and should inform, not settle, dialysis-modality counseling for ADPKD patients who are reasonable PD candidates.

evolution.note: New finding from Gunning, McGill, Chapman, Garimella (Clin J Am Soc Nephrol, epub 2026-07-31, pm_42536420). Retrospective USRDS cohort of ESKD patients aged >=30 with a cystic-kidney-disease diagnosis, 2000-2021, followed to death or 2023-01-01 (n=53,651 incident ADPKD ESKD patients). Time-dependent modality exposure; Cox models adjusted for age, sex, race, BMI, albumin, hemoglobin, year of incident ESKD, insurance status, comorbidities. 26% of patients received some PD. Over median 75-month follow-up: PD associated with lower mortality (adjusted HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.80-0.88, p<0.001) and higher transplantation likelihood (adjusted HR 1.12, 95% CI 1.08-1.16, p<0.001) vs. HD; both associations strengthened with each additional year. Importance 6/Evidence 5/Novelty 7/Decision 5/Calibration 7 (scan-level scores; deep-analysis assessment concurs). CLASSIFICATION: practice-relevant. WHY IT MATTERS: directly addresses a real counseling question -- ADPKD patients are often considered good PD candidates (young, few comorbidities) but clinicians may be hesitant given concerns about mechanical complications from cyst burden; this is the largest ADPKD-specific PD-vs-HD outcomes dataset to date and the associations run counter to that hesitancy. LIMITATIONS (why confidence is LOW despite large n and patient-important endpoints): retrospective registry design with covariate-adjusted but not randomized modality assignment; confounding by indication is the central threat -- patients selected for PD were systematically younger, more often female, and had lower comorbid burden, and Cox adjustment for measured covariates cannot rule out unmeasured selection on abdominal cyst burden, prior abdominal surgery, or physical/cognitive capacity for self-care dialysis, all of which plausibly drive both PD candidacy and survival independent of any causal PD benefit. The paper's own conclusion language ('PD is a safe and advantageous dialysis option... associated with longer patient survival') states the association more causally than the retrospective design supports. CALIBRATED TAKEAWAY: this is reassuring, hypothesis-supporting observational evidence that ADPKD patients selected for PD do at least as well as those on HD -- it does not establish that switching a given HD-eligible patient to PD would causally improve their survival.

findings.statement: Sodium tetradecyl sulfate sclerotherapy of large, symptomatic renal cysts produces sustained, large-magnitude volume reduction in treated cysts and modest total-kidney-volume reduction in ADPKD, based on the largest retrospective single-arm case series reported to date. This is a symptomatic mass-effect management procedure, not a disease-modifying intervention; the same series recorded declining eGFR and rising creatinine over long-term follow-up, and the published conclusion's framing of 'reduced renal function decline' is not supported by a comparator arm or expected-trajectory benchmark in the available data and should not be repeated as evidence of a kidney-function benefit.

evolution.note: New finding from Copping, Sabovich, Pei, Shlomovitz et al. (Kidney360, epub 2026-07-29, pm_42530878), University Health Network Toronto. Retrospective review of 567 cysts sclerosed with sodium tetradecyl sulfate in 306 ADPKD patients, Nov 2014-Aug 2022, plus a companion porcine bladder model probing mechanism. 495 cysts had adequate MRI follow-up: 99% showed volume reduction at first follow-up (mean 162 days, mean reduction 197cm3/88%+/-16%); at long-term follow-up (mean 1359 days) 80% showed further reduction, 18% stable. Mean TKV fell 371cm3 and height-adjusted TKV fell 224cm3 at final follow-up. HOWEVER, over the same mean 1460-day follow-up, serum creatinine INCREASED by 30.5+/-82.6 (units as reported) and eGFR DECREASED by 8.6+/-14.9 mL/min/1.73m2 -- i.e., kidney function declined in absolute terms during the study period. The published conclusion states sclerotherapy 'is associated with reduced renal function decline,' but the abstract as available provides no untreated comparator arm or expected-natural-history benchmark against which to judge whether the observed decline is 'reduced' relative to anything -- this is a headline-vs-evidence mismatch per the evaluation framework's skepticism triggers (single-arm, retrospective, baseline-only design) and is flagged in this cycle's Skepticism Notes rather than taken at face value. Porcine bladder model showed epithelial denudation and superficial inflammation without deep mural injury, supporting a plausible mechanism for the volume-reduction effect specifically (not the renal-function claim). Importance 5/Evidence 4/Novelty 7/Decision 4/Calibration 6 (scan-level scores) -- deep-analysis calibration would score nearer 4/10 given the identified claim/evidence mismatch on the renal-function conclusion specifically. CLASSIFICATION: practice-relevant for symptomatic mass-effect management only; NOT evidence of disease modification. LIMITATIONS: retrospective, single-center, single-arm, no comparator or untreated-cohort benchmark; addresses symptomatic large-cyst mass effect, not a general ADPKD disease-modifying claim. CONFIDENCE: low, pending any comparative study.
